messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the 2/16 runtime change to kernel-selector heuristics, we're seeing steady KV cache memory growth on int8 models under longctx workloads. Repro in prod-sim run A03.
maya: ugh. is it only int8? bf16/bf16-xform seem fine?
alex: bf16 looks stable. int8 shows ~12% higher resident set over 20k tokens compared to previous baseline. Not a single spike — slow growth.
samir: can you paste the profiler snapshot (allocs & slabmap)?
alex: Paste: 
```
# perf sample (summarized)
slot_alloc_calls: 3.2k
slot_free_calls: 1.9k
evict_ops: 2.1k
page_reclaim_attempts: 480
page_shadow_events: 210
kv_reuse_hits: 48% -> down 9pct
```

alex: Notice the "page_shadow_events" entry — looks like slots get partially reused but keep creating tiny fragments that never fully compact.
lina: page_shadowing? is that the thing where evicted page ranges still have some live offsets so we allocate new pages instead of coalescing?
alex: yep. combined with int8 slot packing, fragmentation leads to a lot of micro-pages. memory-efficient but prevents reuse because slot headers don't match contiguous layout.
maya: any perf degradation and/or accuracy delta noted?
alex: accuracy delta is small but measurable on a few eval prompts: avg token logprob down ~0.6% on int8 compared to bf16 baseline in this workload. That is within tolerance but the customer-facing p95 latency also creeps up due to extra page churn.
perf-bot: Regression detector: kernel-selection change #627 triggered on 2026-02-16 — potential correlation score 0.63.
samir: hmm correlation isn't causation. can we repro locally with slower scheduling? try: `RUNTIME_KV_PACK=packed RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREF=fast_gemm ./run_infer.sh --longctx 25000`
alex: ran that exact command, repros reliably in ~2h. I added debug logging for slabmap: `SLOT(id=0x7f4, off=512, size=512, quant=INT8, state=used)` repeated many times.
lina: quick thought: kernel selector now prefers a new fused-int8 attention kernel that returns slightly different slot alignment (8-byte vs 16-byte). That could shift headers by one word and break coalescing assumptions.
maya: can we force fallback kernel in config to confirm?
alex: Yes. I tested `RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREF=fallback` — memory growth stops, reuse hits recover to +8%, page_shadow_events drop to single digits. latency goes back down.
samir: ok that strongly implies the fused-int8 kernel's allocation alignment changed. If so, two fixes: 1) make kernel maintain previous alignment contract, or 2) make slabmap coalesce tolerant to different alignments. Which is lower risk?
lina: making slabmap tolerant is safer long-term but requires careful tests. Also quantify perf delta if we coalesce more aggressively — might add per-allocation overhead.
maya: can we simulate expected overhead? perf-bot, run a quick microbenchmark for coalesce-on-alloc vs strict coalesce across 1M allocs.
perf-bot: queued microbench: coalesce-on-alloc vs strict -> ETA 18m.
alex: I pushed a short-term patch to prefer fallback kernel for int8 on the canary pool (config flag). Canary shows no growth after 6h. Rolling to more pods now.
samir: longer term: update kernel ABI to document alignment, then add unit tests to slot coalescer to accept alternative alignment offsets. Also add a diagnostic counter for "alignment-mismatch" to catch regressions early.
lina: agreed. also add an automated litmus: run 50k token sim, assert reuse_hits >= 40% for int8.
maya: I'll own the canary rollout and metrics dashboard. alex, please attach the repro script and the failing corpus to the ticket.
alex: created ticket INF-9832 with logs and repro script, link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-9832
alex: repro script: `./scripts/repro_kv_growth.sh --model gpt-medium-int8 --longctx 25000 --kernel fused-int8`
maya: thx. If we need to opt customers back to bf16 or fallback kernel, ops needs a toggle. I'll add a runtime feature flag for dedicated/dp.
samir: for the kernel team, this is a friendly reminder: kernel selection must preserve alloc alignment or we need a compatibility shim.
lina: one more datapoint: quantization packing for int8 reduces per-slot size by ~38% but increases header sensitivity. There's a sweet spot where packing wins only if coalescing stays intact.
alex: action items:
- alex: collect more traces and perf profile (in progress)
- maya: manage canary & ops toggle (in progress)
- samir: draft slabmap tolerance PR + unit tests (WIP)
- lina: validate kernel ABI & propose alignment contract (WIP)
- perf-bot: run coalesce microbench and 12h sim nightly

alex: ping if you need the raw heap dumps — they're on s3: s3://redwood-perf/kv_growth/2001112222_dumps.zip
maya: looping in kernel eng if needed, @samir please tag them on the PR.
infra-bot: Deploy started: canary pool change (fallback-int8) by maya at 2026-02-17T14:12:03Z
maya: canary looks green after 2h. memory stable, latency p95 back to baseline.
alex: marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if growth returns. thanks all :thumbsup:
